Cross-reference GitHub's own bypass ledger (`GET .../rulesets/rule-suites`) for --ruleset-id on --target-branch against erun's gate runs: every push that bypassed --ruleset-id is reported next to whether a PASSED gate run's merge commit exactly matches what actually landed. This is the reconciliation half of erun#1912's recorded decision -- narrowing who may hold the bypass grant is a separate, ops-side change; this command makes every bypass accountable after the fact regardless of who holds it.

Exits non-zero, after printing the full report, when any bypassed push has no matching passed gate run -- an unreconcilable push is loud, never silent.

--dry-run traces the GitHub and platform lookups without sending them.

Usage:
  erun exec reconcile-bypass [flags]

Examples:
  erun exec reconcile-bypass --remote-url https://github.com/sophium/erun.git \
    --ruleset-id 11081432 --target-branch main

Flags:
      --dry-run                Resolve and trace mutating actions without executing them.
      --erun-alias string      erun platform cloud alias to target (defaults to the sole configured erun-type alias)
  -h, --help                   help for reconcile-bypass
      --remote-url string      The github.com remote the ruleset lives on (required)
      --ruleset-id int         The ruleset to check bypasses against (required)
      --since string           Narrow the GitHub lookup window: hour, day, week, or month (defaults to GitHub's own window)
      --target-branch string   The ruleset's protected branch (required)

Global Flags:
      --output string   Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time            Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count   Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.
